original_question: Is the sequence ({(3/2)^n})_{n>=0} uniformly distributed in the interval [0,1), or is it not uniformly distributed?
target_in_paper: Section 4, "Miscellaneous problems", unnumbered bullet beginning "Or the still open question:"—the paper asks whether the sequence of powers of 3/2 modulo 1 is uniformly distributed in [0,1). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right sequence, the right ambient interval [0,1), and the right yes/no uniform-distribution problem, and it stays on the exact unnumbered open question in Section 4 rather than drifting to nearby discrepancy-order or Mahler-type problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
missing_details: The paper's question is necessarily modulo 1: one must ask about the fractional parts {(3/2)^n}, or equivalently ((3/2)^n mod 1), since the raw powers (3/2)^n are not themselves a sequence in [0,1) for n >= 1. Section 1 frames the paper throughout in terms of sequences in the unit cube, and Section 4 places this question among those uniform-distribution problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

To be fully stand-alone, "uniformly distributed in [0,1)" should be unpacked in the standard interval-frequency sense used in Section 1: for every interval [a,b) ⊂ [0,1), the limiting proportion of terms falling in [a,b) should equal b-a. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The indexing convention should be fixed explicitly (for example n >= 0, matching your draft); the paper's bullet states the problem without spelling out the starting index. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

No additional ambient ring/field, degree restriction, homogeneity condition, or nilpotency hypothesis is part of this paper-critical statement; this is a one-dimensional distribution-mod-1 problem, so adding such structure would move away from the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
refined_question: Decide whether the sequence of fractional parts ({(3/2)^n})_{n >= 0}, equivalently (((3/2)^n mod 1))_{n >= 0}, is uniformly distributed in [0,1); that is, whether for every interval [a,b) ⊂ [0,1), one has lim_{N -> infinity} (1/N) * #{0 <= n < N : {(3/2)^n} in [a,b)} = b-a.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if D_N := sup_{0 <= a < b <= 1} |(1/N) * #{0 <= n < N : {(3/2)^n} in [a,b)} - (b-a)| denotes the one-dimensional discrepancy of the first N terms, does D_N -> 0 as N -> infinity? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
justification: Section 4 singles this out, in exactly the narrow form your draft is aiming at, as one of the major open questions; it is not presented there as a broader family of problems, nor as Mahler's problem, nor as a discrepancy-order question. Section 1 provides the paper's operative meaning of "uniformly distributed" via discrepancy for sequences in the unit cube. So the faithful sharpening is simply to make the implicit modulo-1/fractional-part operation explicit and to spell out the interval-quantifier that defines uniform distribution. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
